claim_text: KEPCO says an outside cyber intrusion got into its systems and personal data was leaked
summary: KEPCO's own notices of Nov 22 say the leak was caused by a cyber intrusion: features offered for customer convenience became the target of an outside cyberattack, and it detected outside illegal access attempts on KEPCO ON on Nov 20.
detail: The KEPCO ON notice says it blocked the access attempts but found that some customers' data had been leaked in the process. Outlets add that KEPCO 'presumes' an outside attacker broke into both KEPCO ON and the SRM procurement system and took the data. The method and the attacker are not established.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own apology and KEPCO ON notice (Tier 1) state the cyber intrusion and the leak; outlets relay the same company statement.

claim_text: About 1.52 million people's data was leaked across the two systems
summary: KEPCO says 650,487 KEPCO ON users and 869,761 SRM users were affected, which adds up to 1,520,248.
detail: KEPCO has not published a de-duplicated count: Chosunbiz and Electronic Times both say people may appear in both systems. Yonhap (Korean) says KEPCO ON has about 9.2 million users, so the leak there is about 7.1% of them.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The figures are KEPCO's, relayed by several outlets; the true number of distinct people is not given.

claim_text: KEPCO ON customers: IDs, bank accounts, card numbers and billing records leaked
summary: KEPCO's KEPCO ON notice lists the leaked items: customer number, name, resident or foreign registration number, phone, address, bank name, account number, account holder, card company, card number, cardholder, and bills.
detail: The notice says not every item was leaked for every person; customers can check their own case on the KEPCO ON site. Aju Press reports registration and card numbers were stored encrypted (see c012).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own notice (Tier 1) lists the items.

claim_text: Procurement system: names and IDs of company representatives, and staff contact details
summary: KEPCO says SRM exposed names, registration numbers, emails and company addresses of 426,827 company representatives, and names and work contact details of 442,934 KEPCO and company staff.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) says this is every SRM user, and that KEPCO is treating all of them as affected because it cannot pin down each person's exposure.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: KEPCO's breakdown as relayed by outlets.

claim_text: KEPCO learned of it on Nov 20, cut outside access and suspended the services
summary: KEPCO says it found outside illegal access attempts on Nov 20, blocked them, set up an emergency room, reported to the authorities, asked police to investigate and paused some outside services.
detail: KEPCO's apology says it has already asked police to investigate. Seoul Economic Daily gives KEPCO's timeline: it became aware at 6 AM on Nov 20 (Korea), reported to the climate ministry and the National Intelligence Service at 9:31 AM, and asked the Jeonnam provincial police to investigate at 12:31 PM the same day. That settles a difference between early reports: Yonhap (Korean) said it planned to, and Electronic Times said it had.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own apology and KEPCO ON notice (Tier 1) describe these steps.

claim_text: The National Intelligence Service and others are investigating the intrusion
summary: KEPCO says it is working with the National Intelligence Service, the climate and energy ministry and outside security experts to check for further leaks and the scope of harm.
detail: Outlets add that the ministry's cyber safety center is involved and that KEPCO will share details with government and financial authorities. No agency has published findings.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Stated in KEPCO's own apology (Tier 1); no agency statement found.

summary: KEPCO has not said how the attacker got in. Its apology says some features offered for customer convenience and access became the target of an outside cyberattack, without naming them.
detail: KEPCO's line that attacks are getting more advanced, including with AI, is general, not a finding. Yonhap (Korean) quotes KEPCO saying the attacker appears to have pulled records one at a time and then stopped at some point, which is why only part of KEPCO ON's users were hit; KEPCO says the investigation will tell. We found no cause report. News1's report says the leak came to light through slow access and signs on the dark web; it does not name an entry route. Separately, KEPCO's own spring security review had found serious weaknesses (see c017); nothing public ties them to this breach.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: KEPCO's apology names a target area but no method; no cause has been published.

summary: KEPCO and the outlets we read do not identify the attacker. A dark-web forum post claimed to hold KEPCO data (see c013), but that is a claim, not an identification.
detail: This page does not name or guess at an attacker.
label: Not established

claim_text: A separate KEPCO breach in October affected 35,528 people
summary: KEPCO said on Oct 1 that about 24,000 employees' data was exposed on an external webpage. By Oct 23 the count was 35,528, adding retirees and partner staff. Data was names, affiliations and phone numbers.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) and Aju Press report that KEPCO reported it to the privacy regulator and asked the Jeonnam provincial police to investigate. Both cite figures KEPCO gave a National Assembly committee member's office.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets relaying one set of company figures.

claim_text: Whether the Nov 22 breach is linked to the October one
summary: Yonhap (English) calls the October event a separate leak a month earlier. No source says whether the same attacker or the same weakness was involved.
detail: KEPCO says the cause is still being investigated.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing published links or separates the two incidents.

claim_text: No follow-on harm found so far, KEPCO says
summary: KEPCO says no secondary harm has been found so far, and that it will ask government and financial authorities to watch for abnormal transactions on exposed bank and card numbers.
detail: It is early. KEPCO pledges remedies under the Personal Information Protection Act if customers are harmed. Seoul Economic Daily reports KEPCO is working with financial companies to prevent misuse and runs a round-the-clock call center. This claim is about what KEPCO has found, not proof that no misuse exists.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own apology (Tier 1) states no secondary harm found so far.

claim_text: Registration and card numbers were stored encrypted, one outlet reports
summary: Aju Press reports that resident and foreign registration numbers and card numbers were stored in encrypted form.
detail: We did not find this in KEPCO's notices or in other outlets. Encryption at rest does not by itself mean the data cannot be read by an attacker.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relaying KEPCO; not in the company notices we read.

claim_text: A dark-web forum post on Nov 19 claimed to hold KEPCO user and bidding data
summary: DailySecu (Nov 20) and ZDNet Korea (Nov 21) report that a post on a dark-web forum dated Nov 19 claimed to hold KEPCO data: about 590,000 outside users' contact details, internal user records, supplier lists, and bid and contract records.
detail: Both outlets say the post did not name the system or route, and that whether the data really came from KEPCO's SRM was not confirmed. The post came one day before KEPCO says it became aware of the breach. Its figures do not match KEPCO's own counts. We did not visit the forum and do not name the poster. DailySecu's Nov 22 follow-up notes KEPCO's notices do not address the post or whether its data matches what was taken.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets report that the post exists; its contents are the poster's claim and are not verified.

claim_text: Bidding and contract records were also taken
summary: The forum post claimed about 400,000 bid-price records and about 27,000 no-bid contract records. KEPCO told Seoul Shinmun that contract-related data was not leaked.
detail: KEPCO's own notices list only personal data. No other source supports the poster's claim about contract records.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: Only the poster claims it; KEPCO denies it, per one outlet.

claim_text: Power supply is not affected, the climate ministry says
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment said the breach is not currently affecting power operations, and that it will widen inspections to other state-owned energy companies.
detail: We did not find the ministry's own statement. The breached systems are a customer service platform and a procurement system, not grid control systems.
label: Reported

claim_text: The leak came to light through slow access and signs on the dark web, News1 reports
summary: News1's Nov 22 report says the breach surfaced through access delays and dark-web indications.
detail: This matches KEPCO's account that it detected outside illegal access on Nov 20, and the dark-web post press reported on Nov 19 (c013). We could read News1's headline and subhead but not the full article text. It says how the breach was noticed, not how the attacker got in.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reporting how the breach was noticed; not confirmed by KEPCO.

claim_text: KEPCO's own security review this spring found 218 'severe' weaknesses
summary: Money Today (Oct 19), citing KEPCO documents obtained by a lawmaker's office, reports KEPCO's April to July 2026 self-review rated 218 weaknesses severe: 197 on its servers, 21 in public-facing services.
detail: All 10 main public services tested had at least one severe weakness, mainly weak user authentication, weak access-rights checks and exposure of important data. KEPCO planned fixes through autumn; whether they were done is not public. Nothing public says any of these weaknesses was used in either breach.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relaying KEPCO's own audit documents.
